data.about: A point load F on a simply supported beam. A grey trial funicular finds the division point c on the load line — the split of the reactions — and the shear diagram is nothing but the horizontal projection of the levels a, c, b below the beam. Placing the pole o at distance H left of the load line at the level of c makes the closing line horizontal, and the funicular polygon drawn from the baseline becomes the bending moment diagram: M(x) = H · y(x).

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: a simply supported beam A–B — the dotted verticals through the supports will organize the beam, the V-diagram and the M-diagram above each other
steps.title: The beam

steps.caption: left: the point load F on the beam at C, with its line of action — right: F laid off downward on the load line, from a to b
steps.title: The load — in both diagrams

steps.caption: right: place a trial pole o′ anywhere, with grey rays to the ends a and b of the load line
steps.title: Trial pole o′

steps.caption: left: start at D anywhere on the left support vertical and draw parallel to ray a–o′, up to the line of action of F
steps.title: Trial string 1

steps.caption: left: continue parallel to ray o′–b to the right support vertical → K
steps.title: Trial string 2

steps.caption: left: dashed closing line K–D — right: the parallel to it through o′ cuts the load line at c: the division point of the reactions, the same for ANY trial pole
steps.title: Closing the trial → point c

steps.caption: right: c splits the load line: A_V = c→a and B_V = b→c, offset beside it — left: the same forces push up at the supports
steps.title: Reactions A_V and B_V

steps.caption: left: below the beam, a baseline at the height of c — the shear V(x) will be read between the horizontal projections of the load-line points a, c and b
steps.title: V-diagram — the baseline

steps.caption: left: from A to C the shear is constant, +A_V: the strip between the baseline (level c) and level a — right: exactly the reaction segment c→a
steps.title: V-diagram — left of the load

steps.caption: left: at C the load F drops the shear by F to −B_V (level b); at B the reaction closes it back to the baseline — right: the segment b→c
steps.title: V-diagram — right of the load

steps.caption: right: choose the pole distance H, horizontally to the left of b — it will become the scale of the moment diagram
steps.title: Pole distance H

steps.caption: right: go up from M to the height of c → pole o; because o sits at the level of the division point c, the closing ray o–c is horizontal
steps.title: The pole o

steps.caption: left: the baseline L₁–L₂ under the beam: the funicular polygon through both supports will close on this horizontal — the dual of the horizontal ray o–c
steps.title: M-diagram — the closing line

steps.caption: right: ray from o to a — left: from the baseline at the left support, draw funicular string 1 parallel to it, up to the line of action of F
steps.title: String 1 — form and force

steps.caption: right: ray from o to b — left: string 2 parallel to it returns exactly to the baseline at the right support: the funicular polygon closes
steps.title: String 2 — form and force

steps.caption: left: the ordinate y(x) between the closing line and the funicular polygon, measured at ten stations — right: every string was drawn under the pole distance H
steps.title: The funicular ordinates y

steps.caption: left: each ordinate is scaled by H (× the force scale) and mirrored below the baseline: the bending moment M(x) = H · y(x), drawn on the tension side
steps.title: M = H · y

steps.caption: left: connecting the scaled ordinates gives the bending-moment diagram: linear on both sides of the load, maximum right under it — M_max = A_V · |AC|
steps.title: The M-diagram

steps.caption: drag C, B, o′, D, the pole o or the sliders — the V- and M-diagrams follow; click a funicular node (or use the node slider) to read its equilibrium
steps.title: Internal forces from the funicular
